skill.name: python-scripting
skill.description: Create standalone Python scripts that use uv and PEP 723 metadata for inline dependencies, reproducible execution, and CLI structure.
skill.summary: Build self-contained Python utilities with uv, inline dependencies, argument parsing, and reproducible script metadata.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent or prompt injection was found in the reviewed files. The static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and a documentation URL. The skill does guide uv-based scripts that may install dependencies, so users should review packages before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - `references/UV_SCRIPT.template.py` - Python script template with PEP 723 metadata

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL points to official uv documentation inside a Requirements docstring. It is not used for a network request or data transfer.
The flagged text is inline Markdown formatting for a reference file path. It does not execute a command or construct shell input.
The range is a Markdown fenced Python example showing PEP 723 metadata. It is documentation, not runtime shell execution.
The flagged line is a Markdown code-fence delimiter. It has no executable behavior or command injection path.
The bash block documents a fixed uv run command for user-operated scripts. It does not interpolate untrusted input or execute from the skill file.
The range is Markdown fence closure and general prose about dependency installation. It is not Ruby backtick execution or dynamic shell code.

content.value_statement: Standalone scripts often need repeatable dependency setup and clear command-line structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create uv-based scripts with PEP 723 metadata.
actual_capabilities: Creates standalone Python script outlines using uv script metadata.
Adds PEP 723 dependency blocks with Python version requirements.
Builds argparse-based command-line interfaces with optional input and output paths.
Provides a template with usage examples, verbose output, and exit-code handling.
Encourages reproducible installs through uv exclude-newer dates.
limitations: It does not validate that requested package names are safe or maintained.
It does not pin dependencies unless the user asks for exact versions.
It does not replace testing, packaging, or deployment review.
It assumes uv and Python 3.12 or newer are available.

use_cases.title: Create File Automation Utilities

use_cases.title: Prototype Data Cleanup Scripts

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Script

prompt_templates.title: Add Dependencies and Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone Python script that uses specific third-party packages. Add input and output arguments, verbose mode, and dependency metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Script Reproducible
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my one-off Python script into a uv script with PEP 723 metadata, pinned dependencies, and predictable command-line behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Robust CLI Utility
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-ready standalone Python CLI utility. Include dependency strategy, error handling, exit codes, validation, and reproducibility guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a script that reads a CSV file and writes a filtered report.
output: A uv-based Python script plan with inline dependencies for CSV handling.
Command-line arguments for input path, output path, and verbose mode.
Usage notes that explain first-run dependency installation.

output_examples.input: Convert a data cleanup task into a repeatable utility.
output: A focused script structure with argument parsing and clear exit behavior.
A dependency list suitable for PEP 723 metadata.
Practical review notes for package pinning and local execution.

best_practices: Use exact dependency versions for scripts that run in production.
Review generated dependency lists before running scripts on sensitive machines.
Keep each script focused on one task with clear input and output paths.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated scripts with unreviewed dependencies.
Do not place secrets in inline metadata, command arguments, or examples.
Do not combine unrelated automation tasks into one large script.

faq.question: What is PEP 723?
faq.answer: PEP 723 defines inline metadata for Python scripts, including dependencies and Python version requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. The user or agent still decides when to run a script.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require uv?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow assumes uv is installed for script execution and dependency resolution.

faq.question: Can I use it for production scripts?
faq.answer: Yes, but review dependencies, pin versions, add tests, and check operational requirements first.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. Keep secrets in approved secret stores or environment management outside generated script metadata.
